title: Sell Mineral Rights in Edenborn, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Edenborn, PA | Fayette County
metaDescription: Edenborn is a former Fayette County coal patch community near Fairchance. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, cash offer, no broker.
heroLead: Edenborn was built as a coal patch town near Fairchance, and the small community that remains still sits on the same layered mineral history the coal company left behind.
intro: Patch towns like Edenborn have a particular kind of paperwork legacy: company-issued deeds, often boilerplate, that reserved coal for the company while leaving the fate of oil and gas rights less clearly spelled out. Over a century later, families in and around Edenborn are sometimes surprised to learn they hold no gas rights at all, having been reserved away long before anyone alive today was born, or, just as often, surprised to learn they do own something worth selling.
We do the work of reading those old company deeds carefully and tracing the chain forward, so a Edenborn-area family knows exactly what they hold before we make any offer.

sections.heading: Reading a Coal Company's Original Reservation
paragraphs: The language used in early 1900s coal company deeds around Edenborn varies more than people expect, some reserved coal only, others used broader language covering all minerals, and courts have interpreted those phrases differently depending on era and context. We read the actual recorded document for your specific parcel at the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds rather than assuming based on the general reputation of patch-town deeds.

sections.heading: Flank Ground Near Fairchance
paragraphs: This corner of Fayette County sits on the edge of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway, so operator activity has been more selective here than in the deep-core counties to the west. Whether a specific Edenborn-area section has drawn leasing interest depends on the particular operator's program, which is why we check current permitting before discussing value rather than relying on the county's general reputation.

sections.heading: Small Interests From a Long-Closed Company Town
paragraphs: Edenborn today is a quiet community, but the mineral interests tied to its coal-patch history are still very real, even if small and often forgotten. We regularly buy these modest fractional interests, and for a lot of families, a direct cash offer beats the alternative of tracking a small, irregular royalty for years to come.

faqs.question: My family's Edenborn property was a coal company house originally. Do we own any gas rights?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the specific reservation language in the original company deed. We read the actual document rather than assuming based on the town's general history.

faqs.question: Is Edenborn near active Marcellus development?
faqs.answer: It sits on the flank of the wet-gas core, so activity is selective. We check recent permitting for your specific section before discussing value.

faqs.question: Is a small interest from an old patch town even worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. We regularly buy small fractional interests tied to former coal-patch communities like Edenborn.
